text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said Egypt will enter the next century with great confidence that it will exert the utmost effort to increase investment and employment opportunities. But he added that there were some sectors which it was not possible to privatise. "Exports are our future," the president said in a statement in Al-Ahram.
- Mubarak also said that the relationships between Coptic Christians and Moslems in Egypt were good and that Copts have reached high state positions.
- Three died and 273 were injured in huge shopping mall fire in Heliopolis.
- Somali delegation is to visit Cairo in early September before a Somali national reconciliation meeting.
- 434,000 Arab and foreign tourists came through Cairo airport in May, June and July, an increase over the same period the previous year when it was 300,000.
- Egypt sends a rice shipment to Palestinians in the West Bank.
